HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
Anticipatory Bail Application No. 439 of 2026
28 October, 2026
Aasif --Applicant
Versus
State Of Uttarakhand --Respondent
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Parikshit Saini, learned counsel for applicant.
Mr. Tumul Nainwal, learned A.G.A. with Ms. Sweta
Badola Dobhal, learned Brief Holder for the State of
Uttarakhand.
------------------------------------------------------------------
Hon'ble Pankaj Purohit, J.
Applicant has moved this anticipatory bail
application in connection with FIR No.0322 of 2026
dated 13.09.2026 under Sections 351(3), 352 and 69
of BNS, 2023, registered with P.S. Bahadarabad,
District Haridwar.
2. It is alleged in the FIR that applicant-Aasif
had developed physical relations with informant-victim for the last two years on the false pretext of
marriage. But, now applicant is refusing to marry the
informant-victim.
3. It is contended by learned counsel for
applicant that there is a civil suit pending between
the mother of victim-Vasheela and father of

UKHC010189872026
2026:UHC:9703
2
applicant-Noor Ali, in the court of Civil Judge (Senior
Division), Laksar, District Haridwar, which is
registered as O.S. No.20 of 2026 Vasheela Vs. Noor
Ali. The said Suit was filed by victim's mother seeking
injunction against applicant's father on 21.04.2026.
4. It is further contended by learned counsel
for applicant that only to settle the civil dispute, the
instant FIR has been lodged, not only against the
application but also against his entire family- parents
and two brothers, which is totally false.
5. It is further contended by him that
informant-victim is a divorcee and is 28 years of age
while applicant is unmarried youth and there is no
question of false promise of marriage with informant-victim.
6. Per contra, learned State Counsel submits
that from perusal of FIR, the ingredients of offence is
made out against the applicant, but, he could not
furnish any reason as to why the entire family has
been implicated.
7. In such view of the matter, this Court is of
the opinion that this is a fit case where anticipatory
bail can be granted to applicant.
8. Accordingly, the anticipatory bail
application is allowed. It is directed that in the event
of arrest of applicant Aasif, he shall be immediately
released on anticipatory bail on executing a personal
bond of Rs.30,000/ - and two reliable sureties, each
of like amount, to the satisfaction of Investigating

3
Officer, subject to the following conditions: -
i) Applicant shall cooperate with the Investigating
Agency and he shall make himself available for
interrogation by a police officer as and when
required;
ii) If the charge-sheet is filed, the applicant shall
attend the trial court regularly and he shall not
seek any unnecessary adjournment;
iii) Applicant shall not directly or indirectly make
any inducement, threat or promise to any
person, acquainted with the facts of this case;
iv) Applicant shall not leave the country without
the previous permission of the trial court.
7. It is clarified that if the applicant misuses
or violates any of the conditions, imposed upon him,
the prosecution agency will be free to move the Court
for cancellation of the anticipatory bail.
8. Let a certified copy of this order be supplied
to learned counsel for parties today itself, as per
Rules.
(Pankaj Purohit, J.)
 28.10.2026
PN
